story_text:
PolarPlot is a 3D printable SCARA plotter built around a 5-link parallel mechanism, an Arduino-based control system, and custom software developed specifically for the project.
It can work in 2 different modes: Laser engraver or pen plotter.
Designed for makers, artists, students, and DIY enthusiasts, PolarPlot combines an unconventional mechanical design with an accessible software experience.
Print the parts, assemble the machine, upload the firmware, and start creating.
No expensive CNC machine required. No need to design your own control software from scratch.
Just a 3D printer, a handful of standard components, and your creativity.
## 🎯 Why PolarPlot?
Many DIY CNC projects require specialized mechanical components, complex assembly, or complicated software workflows.
PolarPlot takes a different approach.
Its 5-link SCARA architecture provides an alternative to traditional Cartesian plotters, while its 3D printable structure keeps the project accessible to the maker community.
The project combines:
3D printable mechanics — the structural components are supplied as STL files.
Arduino-based control — built around accessible electronics.
Custom-developed software — designed to make operating PolarPlot straightforward.
Two creative applications — use it as a pen plotter or experiment with low-power laser engraving.
A complete digital kit — including printable files, firmware, software, and assembly instructions.
PolarPlot is more than a drawing machine.
It is an opportunity to build, understand, and experiment with a different approach to desktop motion systems.
## ⚙️ A Different Mechanical Architecture
PolarPlot uses a 5-link SCARA mechanism with parallel kinematics.
Instead of moving a tool along conventional X and Y linear axes, the mechanism uses articulated links to position the tool within its working area.
This architecture gives PolarPlot its distinctive mechanical design and makes it an interesting project for anyone curious about robotics, kinematics, and alternative CNC mechanisms.
The mechanical parts are designed to be 3D printed, allowing you to manufacture the main structure yourself and reproduce components whenever needed.
## 🖊️ One Machine, Two Applications
## Pen plotting
Attach a pen and turn PolarPlot into a drawing machine.
Create illustrations, lettering, geometric patterns, diagrams, generative art, and other vector-based projects.
PEN PLOTTER
Let the machine reproduce your designs while you explore the intersection of digital creativity and mechanical motion.
## 🔦 Low-power laser engraving
PolarPlot can also be configured to experiment with laser engraving.
For this application, we recommend a laser with a maximum optical output power of 250 mW and very slow operating speeds.
LASER ENGRAVER
This configuration is intended for light marking and engraving experiments on suitable materials, not for fast or deep engraving.
Laser performance depends on the material, its surface, the optical system, and the operating parameters. Results will vary.
Laser safety is essential. Never operate a laser without suitable wavelength-rated eye protection and appropriate enclosure and fire precautions. Never leave the machine unattended while the laser is operating. Do not use the laser on reflective, unknown, or potentially hazardous materials.
PolarPlot is primarily a DIY plotting platform, with low-power laser experimentation as an additional application.
## 🖨️ Designed for 3D Printing
One of the central ideas behind PolarPlot is to make the mechanical design accessible using a desktop 3D printer.
The digital kit includes the STL files needed to print the machine's components, together with assembly instructions to guide you through the construction process.
The only special commercial mechanical components required are:
Standard screws and fasteners.
Planetary gearboxes.
The remaining printable mechanical components can be manufactured by you.
Electronics, motors, and other components required by the chosen configuration must also be sourced separately.
This approach keeps the project focused on DIY manufacturing and gives makers the freedom to print replacement parts whenever necessary.
## 💻 Custom Software and Arduino Firmware Included
A machine should be enjoyable to build, but it should also be straightforward to use.
That's why PolarPlot includes custom software developed by our team specifically for the project.
it allows you to generate a freehand drawing or import an external SVG file to draw or cut.
Rather than leaving you to assemble a workflow from unrelated tools, PolarPlot brings together its own software and firmware as part of the digital kit.
Our goal is to make the process of preparing and running a plotting project accessible to beginners while still offering an interesting platform for experimentation.
The software is an important part of what makes PolarPlot different: you receive not only the machine design, but also the tools developed to operate it.
## 🧩 Everything You Need to Build PolarPlot
The digital kit includes:
3D printable STL files for the mechanical components.
Step-by-step assembly instructions to guide construction.
Firmware for the Arduino-based control system.
Custom PolarPlot software developed by our team.
Usage and setup instructions to help you get started.
You provide the 3D printer, electronics, motors, planetary gearboxes, screws, and any additional components specified in the build documentation.
No finished machine will be shipped. The reward is a digital package that lets you manufacture and assemble PolarPlot yourself.
## 🎓 Who Is PolarPlot For?
PolarPlot is designed for people who enjoy making things and discovering how they work.
Makers and DIY enthusiasts.
Arduino and 3D printing enthusiasts.
Students and STEM educators.
Artists and illustrators.
Engineers and designers.
Robotics and CNC enthusiasts.
Creative coders and generative art enthusiasts.
Whether you want to draw with a pen, experiment with motion control, or explore low-power laser engraving, PolarPlot offers a hands-on way to bring digital designs into the physical world.
## 🎁 Digital Rewards
## PolarPlot — Digital DIY Kit
The complete digital package to build your own PolarPlot.
Included:
✅ PolarPlot STL files
✅ Mechanical assembly instructions
✅ Arduino firmware
✅ Custom PolarPlot software
✅ Setup and usage documentation
Print the parts, source the required components, assemble the machine, and start experimenting.
Please note: This is a digital reward. A physical machine, 3D printed parts, electronics, motors, planetary gearboxes, screws, and laser module are not included unless explicitly stated in a specific reward tier.
## 🌱 Digital by Design
PolarPlot follows a distributed manufacturing approach: instead of shipping a finished machine, we provide the digital files that allow you to manufacture the printable components locally.
This means:
No bulky machine to ship.
No product packaging.
No need to transport the printed structure across the world.
Replacement parts can be printed locally when necessary.
Where suitable, you can choose recycled or responsibly sourced filament for your printed components.
By sharing the digital design, PolarPlot gives makers the opportunity to build, repair, and experiment with their own machine.
risks: We believe in being transparent about what it takes to build a DIY machine. 3D Printing and Assembly The quality of the printed components depends on printer calibration, material selection, print settings, and assembly accuracy. Following the recommended printing parameters and assembly instructions will be important for obtaining consistent results. Mechanical Calibration As with other articulated plotting mechanisms, positioning performance depends on correct assembly, calibration, and the mechanical characteristics of the components used. We will provide the available setup and calibration instructions to help backers configure their machines. Electronics and Components PolarPlot requires the specified Arduino-compatible electronics, motors, planetary gearboxes, screws, and other components described in the documentation. These items are sourced separately, so availability and compatibility should be checked before beginning assembly. Software and Firmware The software and firmware are developed specifically for PolarPlot. We will provide the versions and instructions included in the digital reward, together with the information needed to configure the system. Laser Operation Laser engraving introduces additional risks, including eye injury, fire, and hazardous fumes from certain materials. The recommended laser configuration is limited to a maximum optical output power of 250 mW, with very slow operating speeds. Appropriate safety precautions remain essential, and laser results will depend on the material and setup.
